hook_text: A country doctor, a milkmaid and an eight-year-old boy. How did they help defeat one of the deadliest diseases in history?
clip_script: England, 1796. Doctor Edward Jenner notices that milkmaids who catch cowpox, a mild disease from cows, do not seem to catch deadly smallpox. He takes pus from a cowpox sore on a milkmaid's hand and puts it into a cut on the arm of eight-year-old James Phipps. Later, he exposes James to smallpox. James stays healthy. The first vaccine is born. Almost two hundred years later, in 1980, smallpox is declared gone from the world.
visual_style: Whiteboard English farm with cows and a milkmaid, a doctor scratching a boy's arm, then a world map with smallpox dots disappearing one by one until 1980.
mood: Dramatic and hopeful, like a detective story with a happy ending.
pacing: A grim start about smallpox, a careful step-by-step experiment, then a triumphant ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask a parent or caregiver to show you your own vaccination record.
